structured_output.summary: Reapplied E0017. In CompressedMaterialization::CompressComparisonJoin I removed the block that compressed both columns of a single equality condition the same way and put the probe key into probe_compress_bindings. Every condition now goes through GetReferencedBindings, and every probe-side binding is marked as referenced, so join keys are never compressed. Build-side payload compression and aggregate/order/distinct CM are unchanged. EXPLAIN ANALYZE of q09.m0 shows the orders scan now gets `o_orderkey IN BF(l_orderkey)` and reads 2.94M rows (it read 15M before). Full bench, run 1: q09 -14.8%, q04 -10.7%, q03 -6.2%, q05 -5.4%, geomean -1.2%; q02 +8%, q19 +6.6%, q18 +6.1% and q08 +6.1% were slower. Run 2: q02 -20.8%, q14 -14.7%, q09 -13.4%, q04 -12.9%, q03 -12.4%, q07 -10.1%, q13 -6.2%, geomean -5.2%; q18 +15.2%, q19 +13.4% and q22 +5.4% were slower. Separate runs of q18/q19 only: q18 -5.3% and +0.6%, q19 -2.4% and +1.5%.
structured_output.generality: This applies to any hash join whose single equality key on an integer column was compressed by CM because a materializing operator (the hash join build) sat above it. The compress projection between the probe scan and the join gave the probe key a storage offset, and that blocked min/max and Bloom filter pushdown into the probe scan. With the block removed, all such joins get the BF back. The cost: joins with a very large build side lose some memory saving from narrower keys, and aggregates above the join may do their own compression instead.
structured_output.notes: The bench is very noisy: q02 measured +8% in one run and -21% in the next on identical code. q18 was slower in both full runs (+6% and +15%), but in two separate q18/q19 runs it was -5.3% and +0.6%, so it is probably noise. Still, q18 is the template most likely to look like a regression in the harness, because its large lineitem/orders build side loses the narrower keys. If q18 does regress for real, a follow-up could keep key compression when the probe side can't receive join filters, or teach BF pushdown to work through the compress offset (an earlier memory notes exact BF through a CM offset already exists for some paths).
